MX17 tests the ATOMKI ⁸Be claim at 3σ in ~1 day with big plastics; as built ~17 days, and only with a repaired liquid scintillator

⁷Li(p,e⁺e⁻)⁸Be at the 18.15 MeV resonance, 1 µA. Geant4 of the full apparatus around a Li₂O target, with a selection that uses no Monte Carlo truth and an n_TOF-anchored detector response. A fit in opening angle × energy split × energy sum, with unknown structure allowed in the background shape.

3σ at R = 5.8×10⁻⁶, 1 µA, calibrated response with the liquid repaired (ideal Geant4 energies: 8 d). With the liquid as at n_TOF or off, the m_ee fit needs months. Needs 3° MM segments or 0.3 ns TOF against cosmics.

four 75×75×5 cm plastics

The trigger_scint calorimeter option (~€90–140k). Calibrated response; worst shape-error case tried 1.2 d; ideal energies 0.7 d. ~4× faster on CN at 4 µA.

1

Details

Geant4 on the MX17_Full_Geant lnl branch (runs L1–L6, overnight 2026-10-08): X17 at four masses, Born IPC M1/E1 at 18.15, 17.64, 15.1 and 14.6 MeV, γ lines, one live day of cosmics, a chamber/backing scan, for the n_TOF stack as built and with four 75×75×5 cm plastics. Analysis: lnl/sim/lnl_geant.py; write-up lnl/FEASIBILITY_SIM.md; this deck reads lnl/out/geant/*.csv.

The days use counting in the best window (typically 130–165°) and an Asimov template fit over 90–180° with the IPC and γ₁ normalisations free (the M1/E1 mix fixed); with the mix also free the fit is ×2.3–3 slower. Rates and yields are lnl_rates.py.

Details

This block (the next twenty slides, the first a one-slide summary for the n_TOF talk) is the pitch for the 15 Oct talk. Everything after it is the backup: the full feasibility study. The days come from lnl/out/geant/reach_geant.csv column days_3d (FEASIBILITY_SIM.md §14.5): Geant4 of the full apparatus around a Li₂O 300 µg/cm² target, a selection with no Monte Carlo truth, the per-layer calorimeter response anchored on the n_TOF measurements, and an event-level Fisher fit in opening angle × energy split × energy sum with the M1/E1/γ₁ normalisations, the anisotropy, a cubic acceptance and Gaussian-process structure all free. The programme total assumes 1 day of setup and 1 day of 441 keV calibration; both are allowances, not computed.

Possible measurement at LNL

⁷Li(p,e⁺e⁻)⁸Be with the MX17 apparatus: 3σ at the ATOMKI ratio in ~1.0 day with big plastics, ~17 days with the n_TOF stack. Geant4, hover for details.

⁷Li(p,e⁺e⁻)⁸Be: ATOMKI's own reaction

A proton beam on lithium, not neutrons on ³He. DC protons at E_p = 1.04–1.10 MeV from the LNL Van de Graaffs (AN2000 / CN) on a thin Li₂O film: the same reaction, energy and target thickness as ATOMKI 2016.

An exact re-measurement with an independent detector. One E_p fixes E* = 18.15 MeV, so the X17 edge sits at 133–139°; the Micromegas tracks point each lepton back to the target and reject cosmics.

A cleaner problem than n_TOF. No neutrons below E_p = 1.88 MeV; a 1.5 µm film instead of a 500 bar capsule (σ68 4.6° instead of 14.5°).

Time to the ATOMKI sensitivity

Big plastics = more trigger acceptance, nothing else. One 75×75×5 cm plate per arm replaces the two bars and the liquid: X17 pairs triggered 3.3 % → 23 % (×7), X17/day ×8, days ÷17.

≈ €93k for four polystyrene plates (€54–142k), ~€121k with the SiPM readout. Budgetary, no labour or VAT.

To study

Scattering in the beam pipe and target chamber smears the edge: 3σ goes 1.0 → 2.5 → 6.8 d as σ68 goes 4.5° → 9° → 14°. Needs the real LNL beam-line drawings in Geant4.

Calorimetry: the 5 cm plates must measure E_sum and the energy split |y| to separate the 15.1 MeV γ₁ IPC (2× the 18 MeV line) and test the background shape. Bench-test a plate.

The X17 record contradicts itself; ⁸Be at LNL is where an independent detector can check it

Left: what has been seen and not seen. Right: what the MX17 apparatus brings to ATOMKI's reaction. Hover the boxes.

The record, as of Oct 2026

ATOMKI 2016, 2022: a 6.8σ excess at ~140° in ⁸Be (1.10 MeV), then excesses at every off-resonance energy (direct capture). Also ⁴He and ¹²C.

Hanoi 2024: ≥ 4σ at 1.225 MeV, with a two-arm spectrometer built by ATOMKI.

MEG II 2025: nothing. R(18.1) < 1.2×10⁻⁵ at 90 % CL; the ATOMKI value has p = 6.2 %.

MEG II members, Sept 2026: cosmic two-arm coincidences make a 140° bump in ATOMKI-type geometries.

LNL 2023–24: an ATOMKI-like spectrometer already ran this reaction on the AN2000. Unpublished.

Two weeks on AN2000 cover the whole programme

Beam days per step: 5σ on the 18.15 MeV resonance, 3σ at both off-resonance energies, setup and the 441 keV calibration; ~4 days on CN at 4 µA. Geant4 reference fit; hover the blocks.

One fixed energy per day suits a self-service AN2000: each setting is held for days. The off-resonance points test the X17 claim directly: the edge moves with E_p, an IPC artefact would not.

With the n_TOF hardware as built the on-resonance 5σ alone takes ~5 weeks, and needs a liquid scintillator that worked at n_TOF only in part. The big plastics are what make it a two-week proposal.

Details

Days to 3σ at R(ATOMKI) from reach_geant.csv (days_3d: θ × |y| × E_sum fit, calibrated response, S_θ 2 % + S_θy 1 %, DAQ live time included); 5σ = 3σ days × 25/9. On resonance is the 'ATOMKI 2016, 18.15 res' target (Li₂O 300 µg/cm² at 1.04 MeV); the off-resonance points are the ATOMKI 2022 (LiF 300, 0.80 MeV) and Hanoi 2024 (LiF 300, 1.225 MeV) configurations. Setup and 441 keV calibration are one-day allowances each (the calibration scaled with current); they are not computed. The off-resonance reach assumes the same R as on resonance, which is ATOMKI's claim.

Details

The n_TOF column is the 2026 campaign as measured and as simulated (MX17_Full_Geant; nTof_x17 sept26_prelim_analysis/). The data-taking ended on 10 Aug 2026; the analysis is still in progress, and its open items are the angle-scale calibration and the reconstruction of two tracks in one chamber. The LNL column is the Geant4 study in this deck. The n_TOF yield question (the ³He self-shielding in the rate table, IPC_MISSING.md item 1) is not listed: it does not change the comparison.

What n_TOF taught us is built into the LNL design

Each n_TOF difficulty (red) and what the LNL setup does about it (green).

The target sets the resolution

The capsule wall smeared the X17 edge into a 40°-wide bump (σ68 14.5°).

→

A 1.5 µm film in a 0.4 mm carbon chamber: σ68 4.6°. The edge stays a step.

The target makes its own background

Neutron capture in the Al/C capsule made pairs 10⁴–10⁶ × more often than ³He.

→

Protons below 1.88 MeV make no neutrons. The background is the reaction's own IPC, which QED predicts.

A white beam smears the kinematics

Each neutron energy has its own X17 edge, 110° → 66°.

→

One proton energy, one edge. Moving E_p on purpose is the test.

The trigger saw a few % of pairs

Two 20×30 cm bars per arm tagged 3.3 % of X17 pairs.

→

Four 75×75×5 cm plates: 23 %, and a calorimeter for |y| and E_sum.

Close tracks merge

Pairs in one chamber below ~12 mm were not reconstructed as two.

→

At 140° the leptons are always in different arms.

Calibration was improvised

The angle scale is still being fixed from muons and the capsule.

→

Calibration lines on tap: the 441 keV resonance, the γ lines, and cosmic MIPs from the single-arm trigger.

n_TOF was not wasted: its measured scintillator response anchors every LNL energy in this study, its cosmics calibrate the arms, and its reconstruction is the one LNL would run.

Details

Drawings as the 'Configs' backup slide (MX17_Full_Geant SimConfig.hh). The plate is 78 cm square, 5 cm thick, front at 41 cm (where the bars are now); the Geant4 runs use 75×75×5 cm. 5 cm of plastic stops most of a ~10 MeV lepton, so the plate is also the calorimeter that the energy split |y| and E_sum need; 2 cm bars stop neither lepton (FEASIBILITY_SIM §14.2). Read each plate at both ends (2 × 3" PMTs through fishtail guides): one end gives 15 % non-uniformity and a 1.5–1.8 ns time offset across the plate (trigger_scint/TRIGGER_OPTIONS.md §4).

Price (budgetary, k€): Budgetary, 2026, no labour or VAT (trigger_scint/costs.py): four 78×80×5 cm slabs with two 3" PMTs each, fishtail guides, wrapping, mechanics, HV and digitizer channels. Polystyrene €93k (54–142k); cast PVT €136k (78–217k). Plus reading all 20 SiPM bars (~€10k) and the SiPM DAQ (next-but-one slides). Get two vendor quotes before deciding.

Weight: ~32 kg per plate, so the arm frames need rework. Confirm the largest single-piece 5 cm sheet with the vendor; the fallback is two 37×75 cm bars per arm (+2 PMTs per arm, ~+€50k in all).

At LNL the limit is signal-to-background, not statistics

Left: the most significance a counting analysis can ever reach if the background shape is known to δ (big plastics, best window). Hover the lines.

Statistics are not the problem. One week at 1 µA with big plastics: ~750 X17 on ~10,700 IPC pairs in 130–172°. A 3σ excess is ~1σ per bin.

The cap. If the background shape under the edge is uncertain by δ relative to its sidebands, counting can never beat Z = (S/B)/δ. All pairs at 2 %: 3.9σ, however long we run.

What lifts it: the energy split takes S/B from 8 % to 19 %, and the fit in θ × |y| × E_sum measures the shape from the signal-free parts of the data. With realistic shape errors it slows by at most ×1.2.

So the study list is about the background shape, at the 1 % level: next slides.

lnl/out/syst/ycut.csv; lnl/out/nd/nd_days_*.csv; FEASIBILITY_SIM §11–14

10

Details

S/B in the best window from lnl/out/syst/ycut.csv (big plastics, MM 15° + TOF, ideal energies; as built is the same within ±1 %). The cap Z_max = (S/B)/δ is for a uniform fractional error δ on the background in the window relative to the sidebands (FEASIBILITY_SIM §11–12). The fit numbers (§14.3, calibrated response) are not capped this way because the fit measures the shape: worst structure tried 1.2 d against 1.0 d nominal (big plastics), 21 against 17 d as built. Those numbers hold only if the true shape error looks like the Gaussian-process structure assumed (5 % at most, correlation length ≥ 5°).

One week of pairs in the plane of opening angle × energy split

Big plastics, 1 µA, 7 days, E_sum 14–19 MeV, calibrated response, MM 15° + TOF (Geant4). Dashed: where a 16.7 MeV X17 lands. Hover any cell.

Raw counts. ~23,000 background pairs in the window this week, spread over every |y|; ~650 X17. In the 1D spectrum at 125–155° that is S/B ≈ 8 %: a background shape error of a few % competes with the signal.

The X17 is a line, not a bump. A particle of fixed mass reaches the smallest angle only when the leptons share the energy equally, so its pairs follow the constant-mass curve. The IPC is a virtual photon of any mass: it fills the plane.

S/B in 2D. The best 5 % of cells reach S/B ≈ 23 %; at |y| < 0.3, 125–155° it is 13 %. Everything off the curve is background-only: the fit measures the background shape there, in the same run.

lnl/out/nd/maps/maps.csv (lnl/sim/lnl_nd_maps.py)

11

Details

lnl/sim/lnl_nd_maps.py → lnl/out/nd/maps/maps.csv (FEASIBILITY_SIM §16). The event list is the reference fit's (lnl_nd.collect): Geant4 L1 (X17 m = 16.7 MeV, at R(ATOMKI)), L2 (IPC M1, E1 and γ₁), L3 (EPC), L4 (cosmics), big plastics, MM 15° + TOF, the n_TOF-anchored calibrated response, E_sum window 14–19 MeV, 1 µA, live-corrected. Cells are 3° × 0.05. Each lepton must reach the plastic to make a trigger leg, so neither carries less than a few MeV: that is the top edge of the background near |y| ≈ 0.8. The background map is KDE-smoothed in θ (5°) as in the fit; the X17 map is not. Cells with fewer than one background pair (left) or three (right) are blank. The calibrated response smears |y| (measured energies, partial containment), so the X17 band is wider than the ideal curve. Compare the backup slide "Why |y|", which shows S/B for ideal energies.

The reference fit uses this plane with E_sum as a third axis (two side-band bins, two window bins): 45 θ bins × 6 |y| bins × 4 E_sum bins.

A background error can fake the angle, not the energies

Excess above the background model in 7 days, big plastics, 1 µA. Red: X17 at the ATOMKI ratio. Orange dashed: an "impostor", a background error built to match the X17 angle spectrum exactly. Grey: ±1σ statistics.

X17 (ATOMKI ratio)

impostor: background error

±1σ background statistics

In angle alone they are identical, by construction. Any 1D analysis, ours or ATOMKI's, cannot tell a real X17 from a background shape that is a few % wrong under the edge.

Energy split: 74 % of the X17 is at |y| < 0.3, against 45 % of the impostor. A background error has the background's energy sharing; the X17 has its own.

Energy sum: an acceptance or efficiency error does not know the lepton energies, so it appears in the 15 MeV γ₁ side band too: ×2.5 its window size there, against ×0.4 for the X17.

lnl/out/nd/maps/proj.csv (lnl/sim/lnl_nd_maps.py)

12

Details

lnl/sim/lnl_nd_maps.py: the impostor takes every X17 event (E_sum window) with its reconstructed angle and gives it the |y| and E_sum of a background event at the same angle (±1.5°, 30 draws each). Its angle spectrum in the window is the X17's exactly; its energy sharing and energy sum are the background's. This is impostor A ("acceptance"): a geometry, material or efficiency error, which is the same at every lepton energy, so it also appears in the γ₁ side band with the background's weight there. Impostor B (an error only in the 18 MeV IPC physics, absent in the side band) is on the next slide.

The X17 also leaks into the side band (the calibrated response smears E_sum: part of each lepton escapes the plate). The fit models that; it is in the X17 template.

In 2D the X17 is a spot and a background error is a stripe

Local significance per 6° × 0.1 cell after 7 days, big plastics, 1 µA: the X17 (top) and the impostor of the last slide (bottom), in the E_sum window (left) and the γ₁ side band (right). Hover the cells and bars.

How much of the impostor each fit calls X17 (7 d)

angle alone

100 %

pair mass m_ee

18 %

angle × split

14 %

angle × split × sum

13 %

The angle-only fit is fooled completely: it reads the impostor as 100 % of an X17, exactly as significant as the real thing however long we run. The 2D and 3D fits report ≤ ¼ of it (~1σ in a week), while a real X17 is 7.5σ.

And the data say so. The impostor leaves χ² ≈ 20 the 3D fit cannot absorb in a week (≈ 0 in 1D): the excess sits at high |y| and in the side band, where no X17 can be.

What no fit catches: a background error that is symmetric, at the edge and only at 18 MeV, i.e. shaped like the X17 in all three. An error only in the 18 MeV IPC physics (impostor B) still reads as 24 %. The checks for that are physics: QED fixes the IPC shape, and the X17 edge moves with E_p (441 keV, off-resonance) where a detector effect does not.

lnl/out/nd/maps/maps.csv, bias.csv (lnl/sim/lnl_nd_maps.py)

13

Details

lnl/sim/lnl_nd_maps.py → maps.csv (coarse grid) and bias.csv. The bars are the linear (Asimov) response of each fit to a background model that is wrong by the impostor: the fitted X17 strength moves by (T F + P)⁻¹ T Σ g Δ/μ, with F, P the fit's Fisher and prior matrices after T = 7 days, g the parameter derivatives and Δ the impostor. The fits are the reference ones (lnl_nd.py): M1, E1, γ₁ norms, anisotropy, θ and |y| resolution, E scale, four arm gains, a free acceptance cubic in θ, a |y| tilt, and unknown structure S_θ 2 % + S_θy 1 %. The impostor is as large as the X17 itself at the ATOMKI ratio. "χ² left" is the part of Σ Δ²/μ the free parameters cannot absorb, i.e. the Asimov goodness-of-fit penalty for the wrong model; over ~1000 bins a Δχ² of 20 is not a subtle effect but not a single-bin alarm either.

Impostor B (an error confined to the 18 MeV window, every |y|): 24 % in the 3D fit, +1.8σ, χ² left 17. With no structure terms at all, the 3D fit reads impostor A as 21 % (the angle-only fit 100 %): the |y| and E_sum axes do most of the work, not the Gaussian-process freedom.

Why n_TOF could not do this: the edge was smeared to σ68 14.5° by the capsule, the excitation energy changes with the neutron energy (no fixed E_sum line, no signal-free side band from the same reaction), the arms contained ~40 % of the lepton energy, and the background was neutron capture in the capsule, whose shape QED does not predict. So the n_TOF search had to rest on the opening angle, the top bar.

STEP 1 OF 4 · THE DATA

One simulated week, as the experiment would record it

7 days, 1 µA, big plastics. The X17 is in at the ATOMKI ratio, and the true background differs from our Monte Carlo in ways the fit is not told. Hover the cells and points.

~24,000 pairs in the window and ~52,000 in the 15 MeV side band. The dashed curve is where an X17 would land. By eye: nothing.

How the "truth" differs from our model: the IPC and γ₁ normalisations by ~10 %, the acceptance by 3 % per term, every nuisance within its prior. On top of that, 2 % shape errors in angle × energy sum and in pair mass that the fit does not contain at all.

In 1D the raw Monte Carlo (grey) does not describe the data at the few-% level. The X17 is a ~10 % bump on this, so we cannot just subtract the simulation.

lnl/out/pseudo/walk_bins.csv (lnl/sim/lnl_pseudo.py)

14

Details

lnl/sim/lnl_pseudo.py (FEASIBILITY_SIM §17). Pseudo-data: Poisson draws in θ (2°) × |y| (0.05) × E_sum (10–12, 12–14 | 14–16.5, 16.5–19 MeV) from a "truth" built on the reference fit's Geant4 event list (big plastics, calibrated response, MM 15° + TOF). Truth = nominal + random shifts of every background parameter (M1, E1, γ₁ norms σ 10 %; acceptance cubic σ 3 %; anisotropy, resolutions, E scale, arm gains, |y| tilt at their priors; the modelled structure S_θ 2 % + S_θy 1 % at N(0, 1)) + structure the fit does not have: S_θE 2 % and S_m 2 % (ℓ 0.55 MeV), 264 modes in all. X17 at r = 1 (R = R(ATOMKI)), seed 20261015: one pseudo-experiment, not chosen. Display cells are 4° × 0.05.

STEP 2 OF 4 · THE SIGNAL REGION

Zoomed in: a bump at the edge, on a rough background

Same pseudo-data: 116–172°, |y| < 0.6, E_sum window, 2° × 0.05 cells. Middle: the data against the raw Monte Carlo, in standard deviations. Hover.

The X17 shows as an excess along the dashed curve, strongest at 130–140° and small |y|: +284 pairs over the raw MC at 128–146°, |y| < 0.3.

But the raw MC is also wrong elsewhere: blue and red cells away from the curve are the background mismodelling. Subtracting the simulation would give a "signal" of the wrong size, and a 1D analysis could not tell which part is which.

So the background has to come from the data, in the regions where no X17 can be: next step.

lnl/out/pseudo/walk_bins.csv, walk_proj.csv

15

Details

Pull per cell = (data − raw MC)/√MC, with the raw MC the nominal simulation (no X17, no fitted parameters). The injected X17 in the plotted |y| < 0.3 band is in the Details of step 4. Cells with fewer than 2 expected pairs are blank.

STEP 3 OF 4 · BACKGROUND FROM THE DATA

Measure the background where the X17 cannot be

Left: the plan in the E_sum window (orange = blinded; the side band is all control). Middle: the background predicted in the blinded region (blue band) and, because this is a simulation, the truth (green dashed).

What the control regions measured

background in the blinded region2,3492,381 ± 30

Blind first. The 76 cells holding 70 % of the expected X17 are hidden. The background-only fit uses everything else: the γ₁ side band (same acceptance, no 18 MeV transition), the asymmetric pairs, and the angles below the edge.

It predicts the hidden background to 1.3 %, and it is right: 2,381 against a true 2,349 (+1.0σ), even with shape errors it was not told about.

lnl/out/pseudo/walk_proj.csv, walk_summary.json

16

Details

The blinded fit is the reference model with r fixed at 0 and the signal-region bins removed: M1, E1, γ₁ norms and the acceptance cubic free; anisotropy, θ and |y| resolution, E scale, arm gains, |y| tilt and the S_θ 2 % + S_θy 1 % structure with their priors (178 parameters, 1963 bins). The band is the fit covariance propagated to each bin. The S_θE and S_m structure in the truth is not in this model at all.

About 30 % of the X17 falls outside the blinded region (the response smears |y| and E_sum), so the control regions carry a little signal; the blinded fit absorbs part of it into the background. That is why step 4's excess in the blinded region is a little below the injected signal, and why the final number comes from the full fit, which models the signal everywhere.

STEP 4 OF 4 · UNBLIND

Data − background: the X17 returns, r̂ = 0.87 ± 0.14

The background predicted by the blinded fit is subtracted. Points: data − background, ±1σ (data and prediction). Red: the X17 injected. Blue dashed: what the full fit measures.

In the blinded region: 2,708 pairs on a predicted 2,381 ± 30: an excess of 327 ± 60 (5.4σ). The X17 put in there: 458.

The full fit (all bins, signal free): r̂ = 0.87 ± 0.14, 6.1σ, for a true r = 1. The excess sits on the X17 curve at small |y|.

And nowhere else: the asymmetric pairs (right) are flat at zero. Mismodelled background would show there too; an X17 cannot.

Residual = data − blinded-fit prediction; error = √(data + σ²_prediction). The excess in the blinded region is below the injected 458 because the blinded fit absorbs the ~30 % of the X17 that falls in the control regions (step 3 Details); the full fit, which models the signal in every bin, is the measurement: r̂ = 0.867 ± 0.142, 90 % CL upper limit 1.10, χ² 2034 for 1963 bins and 178 parameters (many with priors). One pseudo-experiment; the next slide runs a thousand.

A week works as advertised: the true coupling comes back without bias, r = 1 to ±15 % (ε ∝ √R to ±7 %). Background-only weeks almost never fake 3σ. No X17 → R < 1.3×10⁻⁶ (MEG II: 1.2×10⁻⁵).

Two warnings. At 30 days the statistics are good enough that the 2 % shape errors the fit does not know about dominate: fake 3σ in 1.7 % of months. Floating those shapes too ("wider fit") brings it to 0.2 % at the cost of σ ×1.1. And the template Monte Carlo must be ~10× larger than now: half of it gives a +0.1 offset.

lnl/out/pseudo/scan.csv (lnl/sim/lnl_pseudo.py)

18

Details

lnl/out/pseudo/scan.csv (toys.csv: every pseudo-experiment). Each one draws a new truth (all background parameters, the modelled and the unmodelled structure, as in step 1) and new Poisson data, then runs the full fit. Z = r̂/σ and the 90 % CL upper limit (one-sided, Δχ² = 2.71 from max(r̂, 0)) use the quadratic approximation of the profile likelihood. Coverage of the 90 % upper limit for r > 0 at 7 days: 91–98 %; at 30 days 87–89 % (the pull width again). "Wider fit": the fit also floats the S_θE and S_m structure that the truth contains (the real-life equivalent: let the background model carry every class of shape error the controls cannot rule out). r = R/R(ATOMKI), R(ATOMKI) = 5.8×10⁻⁶; the X17 coupling ε goes as √R, so ε/ε(ATOMKI) = √r.

What is not in here: a background error shaped like the X17 in all three variables (the impostor slides), the MC statistics of a larger-than-simulated γ₁ sample (the "mc halves" row uses half the MC for each side), and any look-elsewhere effect from scanning the X17 mass.

Beam-pipe scattering is the design driver; the 3D fit keeps it survivable

Days to 3σ against the X17 resolution, for four fits with the same background-shape freedom (big plastics, calibrated response). Hover.

opening angle alone

pair mass m_ee

angle × energy split

angle × split × energy sum

The worry is justified. Once the background shape may float, a wider edge looks like background structure. The reference fit goes 1.0 → 2.5 d at 9° and 6.8 d at ~14°, the n_TOF capsule.

The higher-dimensional fit is what keeps it alive. |y| and E_sum come from the scintillators and do not smear. At ~14°: 6.8 d against 28 d for m_ee; the angle alone never gets there.

Design rule: only the wall the leptons cross counts (3.8° of the 4.6° is the CFRP). Accepted leptons fly at ≥ 49° to the beam axis, so flanges, valves and pipe are harmless inside the cone r < 1.1·|z|. A 1 mm stainless pipe crossing the arms would cost ×31 (estimate).

lnl/out/nd/smear_scan.csv (lnl/sim/lnl_smear_nd.py)

19

Details

lnl/sim/lnl_smear_nd.py (FEASIBILITY_SIM §15): every event's reconstructed angle is moved away from its Geant4 truth by a factor f (1, 2, 3.1, 6), so the residual distribution, tails included, scales by f: a stand-in for a thicker wall, not a Geant4 run of one. f = 2 is close to Geant4's Al 0.5 mm chamber (9.0°); f = 6 is a Highland estimate of a 1 mm stainless tube (x/X₀ 5.7 % against Al 1 mm's 1.1 % at 12.2°). Fits as the reference: calibrated response, S_θ 2 % + S_θy 1 % structure (ℓ = 10°), arm gains, free acceptance cubic, θ-resolution scale ±10 %. The old counting estimate (§10: ×1.5 at 14.5°) assumed the IPC shape known exactly; with the shape free the cost is much larger.

The cone rule: the Micromegas active area spans ±180 mm along the beam at 204 mm, so accepted leptons have polar angles 48.6°–131.4° from the beam axis and cross the plane |z| = Z at r ≥ 1.13·Z. They leave the 25 mm chamber within |z| ≤ 22 mm of the target. Flanges, valves and the beam pipe are harmless if they stay inside that cone; a geometric estimate, to be checked with the real LNL beam line in Geant4 (ask for the drawings).

Open issues: the wall, the plates and the IPC shape matter most

Red: can change the answer. Orange: can change the schedule. Grey: to arrange.

Beam line and chamber at LNL (ask)

The thin carbon section must reach ±5 cm around the target, and nothing thick may enter the 49° cone. A 1 mm steel pipe there: ~×30 (estimate).

Big-plate response (bench)

No data on 5 cm plates. Calibrated: 1 d; n_TOF-quality: 2.4 d; poor plates: 5 d.

IPC shape (theory + data)

Born M1/E1 without interference today. The fit with the mix free is ×2–3 slower.

Timing for the cosmic veto (measure)

TOF needs σ_t ≲ 0.4 ns per arm; 0.3 ns is assumed. Else 3° Micromegas segments.

Hall space and mounting (ask)

A ~1.2 m cube around the target with ~1 m clearance; 32 kg plates on reworked frames.

Scintillator DAQ (buy)

n_TOF read the scintillators on its own digitizers, which stay there. Next slide.

Target (ask LNL)

Li₂O lifetime at 1 µA; ¹¹B and ¹⁹F contamination; the backing above 992 keV (²⁷Al(p,γ)).

Beam time

LNL PAC, next call this autumn (ask); AN2000 is the LNL group's machine.

The LNL 2023–24 result

Their AN2000 data may answer part of the question first. Talk to them: partners, not competitors.

Details

From trigger_scint/TRIGGER_OPTIONS.md §5 and trigger_scint/costs.py (budgetary EUR, 2026, no labour or VAT; vendors quote on request). At n_TOF each wall recorded 8 channels (16 of 20 bars ganged in fours, each group summed top and bottom) on the facility's ADQ14 digitizers, and the plastics and liquid on the same; none of those come with us. The study counted one SiPM per bar end (4 walls × 20 bars × 2 ends = 160); if each end has two SiPMs read separately, it is 320 and the FERS option needs 5 units (the price above scales by 5/3, a rough estimate). Ganging the two SiPMs of one end into one channel keeps it at 160.

Timing: the toy ray-trace gives σ_t ≈ 120 ps at 5 MeV for a 78×80×5 cm plate with two 3" PMTs after the Micromegas position correction (optimistic by ~1.5–2×), inside the ≲ 0.4 ns the cosmic veto needs (FEASIBILITY_SIM §7). If the plates give the TOF, the SiPM wall's role in the trigger leg is the coincidence and the position; a plate-only leg would gain ~1.4× in X17 acceptance but take more singles (§8 item 8). The FERS units have trigger-OR outputs, so the SiPM wall can stay in the leg if wanted.

Rates: lnl/out/trigger/prescale_choice.csv (big plastics, ATOMKI 2016 anomaly target, every single-arm trigger taken, DREAM RAW 20 samples, τ = 298 µs).

At 1.1 MeV, half the γ₀ is direct capture, not the resonance

⁷Li(p,γ₀)⁸Be cross section split into the two M1 resonances and a flat E1 direct capture. Hover the points.

total σ(γ₀), Zahnow 1995

M1 resonances

direct E1 capture

52 % of the γ₀ is direct E1 capture in ATOMKI's 2016 anomaly run (Li₂O 300 µg/cm² at 1.10 MeV); the 18.15 resonance makes the rest.

That matters: E1 IPC has ~2.5× the M1 rate at 140°, and ATOMKI 2022 sees its excess in direct capture too.

The 441 keV resonance is 50× stronger and makes 17.64 MeV pairs, where MEG II already limits X17. A thick target walks into it.

lnl/out/figures/excitation.csv (lnl_rates.py). Curves below 1 µb are drawn at 1 µb.

25

Details

Zahnow et al. 1995 (EXFOR A0639) S-factors for γ₀ and γ₀+γ₁, 98–1500 keV, converted to σ. The resonances are Breit–Wigner with constant widths (Tilley 2004); direct capture is the remainder. The split is not meaningful below ~500 keV, where the BW tail and the data disagree, but it is harmless at 1 MeV.

Checks against Tilley: σ(γ₀+γ₁) at 441 keV = 5.93 mb (5.9 ± 0.5); γ₀/(γ₀+γ₁) = 0.69 (0.69–0.72). MEG II's own 2026 normalisation is reproduced when their n and σ are used (factor 2 in the inputs, not the method).

θ_min = 2·asin(m_X/E_X) against E_p, for three masses. Hover the points.

The X17 piles up above an edge at 134–139° at the 18.15 resonance; IPC falls steeply there.

The edge moves by ~10° over the scanned energies, so a real signal must follow it. That is the test the off-resonance points make.

The Geant4 reach uses the window that maximises S/√B (~130–165°) and a template fit over 90–180°; the edge sits inside both for all three masses.

Keep the film thin (≲ 300 µg/cm² ≈ 60 keV of energy loss): then < 1 % of the γ₀ is 17.64 MeV, and the signal sits at 18.15.

A beam that stops in Li metal at 1.10 MeV gets 77 % of its γ₀ from 441 keV. That is what happened to ATOMKI's 2016 targets (Sas 2022).

Use boron-free Li: ¹¹B(p,γ) puts 16–17 MeV γ in the window. LiF gives a free ¹⁹F E0 line (6.05 MeV) for calibration.

Details

An arm is "ok" with a trigger leg (a SiPM bar AND a plastic, each ≥ 0.5 MIP) and a Micromegas segment whose charge centroid is in the active area. Pairs = the two ok arms with most scintillator energy. The arm choice matches the true lepton arms in 99.8 % of X17 events. The accepted X17 spreads from the 134° edge to 170°: the four-arm geometry favours back-to-back pairs, so only ~64 % of the tagged pairs fall in 125–155°. The template fit uses the rest.

29

Details

The pre-Geant4 estimate assumed the n_TOF stack (~40 % containment) could not separate the γ₁ transitions (to the 3.0 MeV state, W ≈ 15 MeV, twice as frequent as γ₀) and counted their IPC in full. Geant4 says the LS make the difference: with them, nothing from 15.1 MeV reaches 13 MeV. The LS suffered pile-up at n_TOF; at LNL the rates are ~10³× lower, but whether they can be read is to be checked (ask). "As built, LS off": the window cannot exclude γ₁, and the reach goes from 15 to 19 days.

30

Details

Cosmic μ± from a 3×3 m plane, 1 /cm²/min, zenith perpendicular to the beam (sea level, no overburden). MEG II members showed in 2026 that cosmic two-arm coincidences make a ~140° bump in ATOMKI-type spectrometers; this is that effect quantified for MX17. Entries ≤ 2 are single events in one live day. The pointing cut keeps 90 % of X17 segments per arm (D = 135 mm at 15°, 57 mm at 3°; scattering in the window and gas sets the 3° value). σ_t = 0.3 ns per arm is an assumption (ask): at 1 ns the veto no longer separates the 2.3 ns muon delay. Two-arm cosmic triggers: 3.5/s as built, 22/s with big plastics; DREAM stays > 99 % live.

It is acceptance. The X17 rate goes up ×15, but the IPC goes up ×14 with it, so S/B hardly moves (0.059 → 0.064). Days ∝ B/S² then fall like 1/S: 24 → 1.4 d (×17).

The picture (left): where the leptons that cross a Micromegas land at the plastic. The as-built bars catch 36 % per lepton, so a pair (both legs) ~13 %. 75×75 catches 92 %; with the SiPM wall in front, 83 %.

Details

Factors from the Geant4 chain (lnl/out/plastics/chain.csv, from acceptance_geant.csv and reach_geant.csv): as built with the LS, E_sum 13–17; big plastics, E_sum 13–18; MM 15° + TOF; counting in 125–155°. The stage factors multiply to the X17 gain within a few % (the E_sum windows differ slightly).

Why the background follows: the IPC pairs come from the same spot, in the same arms, with similar energies, so a bigger plastic tags them just as it tags the X17 (Geant4: M1 ×7.6, E1 ×6.8, X17 ×7.1 in pair-tag). With S/B fixed, significance grows as √S: ×15 in rate is ×15 in time.

The map is from the geometric toy (lnl/plastic_size.py): straight leptons from the spot, the surveyed arms, Highland kicks behind the MM, an energy threshold. Fitted to the two Geant4 X17 pair-tags; the IPC big/as-built ratios match Geant4 to ~3 %.

Details

To scale, from the MX17_Full_Geant SimConfig.hh constants (the ones lnl/plastic_size.py uses). Micromegas windows at 204–204.5 mm, 45 mm deep, active 399.4 mm across the arm × 359.9 mm along the beam. The pinwheel shifts each arm 15.5–17.3 mm sideways. The 50×50 cm SiPM wall (20 bars, 3.5 cm container) has its front at ~31.5 cm. The as-built bars' fronts are at 41.1–41.3 cm: two 20×30×2 cm bars side by side, 40 cm across and 30 cm along the beam.

The plate is the optimum of the next slide: 77.5 cm square, 5 cm thick, front at 41.5 cm. Up to ~75 cm the front stays where the bars are (41 cm). Bigger plates touch their neighbours at the corners and must move back. The SiPM wall stays in the trigger leg: its timing is the TOF cut against cosmics, which one large slab would probably do worse (ask). The liquid scintillators behind the as-built bars are not drawn. The big-plastic Geant4 runs have no LS (--big-plastic 75 75 5 --no-ls --sipm-readout 20 0).

Optimum at ~78 cm (1.19 d, 2.4 m² of plastic for 4 arms). Within 10 % of it from ~65 cm (1.7 m²).

It saturates because the 40×36 cm Micromegas set the acceptance: 75 cm already covers their cone at 41 cm.

Past ~75 cm the plates collide (centred square plates touch once S/2 ≳ R − 3 cm), so they move back and lose a little. The footprint is not the limit before the optimum.

lnl/out/plastics/days_vs_size.csv, calib.csv, footprint.csv

35

Details

An analytic stand-in, not Geant4. lnl/plastic_size.py: X17 and Born M1/E1 IPC with the Geant4 generator kinematics, from a σ = 2 mm spot, into the surveyed arms (SimConfig.hh). A leg needs the lepton through the MM active area, a read-out SiPM bar (20 bars) and the plastic face, after Highland kicks behind the MM (x/X₀ = 0.03, fitted) and in the SiPM wall, with KE > 5.25 MeV (fitted). The two numbers fit the Geant4 X17 pair-tags (as built 3.3 %, big plastics 23 %). Refitting with a 3 MeV threshold moves the curve by < 7 %.

Days = 1.2 d × (B/B₇₅)/(S/S₇₅)², counting X17 and IPC (γ₀ mix of the ATOMKI 2016 run) in 125–155° after a 5° smear. The E_sum, MM and TOF efficiencies are held at the Geant4 big-plastic values, so this is geometry only; a thin or small plate would also lose calorimetry. Footprint: plates centred on each arm, fronts at 41 cm from the beam; neighbours touch when S/2 + 1.7 cm (pinwheel) + 1 cm (wrap) > R, then R is increased. The SiPM wall stays where it is (fronts at 31.5 cm) and stays in the trigger leg (it gives the TOF). Other placements (closer, behind the SiPM wall; no SiPM wall) are in days_vs_size.csv but are not considered practical.

To confirm before buying: one Geant4 run with an oversized plate (the --big-plastic option was made for this: cut any smaller plate offline from its hits).

37

Details

The LNL version of the n_TOF capsule "dilution" plot. Truth = the generated opening angle (no scattering, perfect detector). CFRP = the Geant4 reconstructed chord (beam spot → MM centroids) of the same events, with the real chamber (CFRP 0.4 mm, r = 25 mm), Al 10 µm backing, Al 1 mm holder, air, MM window and gas. Al 1 mm: the Geant4 L5 residual distribution (reco − truth) applied to the same truth angles. No-wall and n_TOF curves are Gaussian illustrations (3.5° from the appendix model floor; 14.5° = σ68 at n_TOF).

Days: IPC (γ₀ + γ₁) and X17 at R(ATOMKI) per day, each smeared the same way, best counting window on 2° bins, scaled so the CFRP case = 1.20 d. The edge is sharp in truth (132-150°), so scattering costs ×1.34 overall, of which the wall ~×1.11. Even an n_TOF-like 14.5° would only cost ×1.5: at LNL the IPC under the edge is smooth and the edge sits where the IPC is falling.

How: counting is S/√B in 130-172° with the IPC expectation taken as exact: 1.2 d to 3σ. Freeing the IPC norm (template fit over 90–180°): 1.6 d. Freeing the M1, E1 and γ₁ norms separately: 3.7 d. Statistical only; Z grows as √t.

The catch: S/B ≈ 7 %. An uncertainty ε on the IPC shape under the edge (relative to the sidebands) caps Z at S/(εB): 3.5σ for 2 %, 1.4σ for 5 %. The result needs the IPC angular shape to ~1 %, from the data (sidebands, E_sum) and the Born calculation.

lnl/out/scatter/week.csv, week_z.csv (lnl/sim/lnl_week.py); stacked.csv (lnl_scatter.py); reach_geant.csv

38

Details

751 X17 on 10,719 IPC pairs in 130-172° per week (7.7σ in this pseudo-experiment, 7.3σ expected). Per day at 1 µA, Li₂O 300 µg/cm² at 1.10 MeV, × 7 days × live time: IPC = Born M1 (resonances) + E1 (direct capture) + γ₁ (yields.csv), Geant4 reconstructed chord, smoothed with the 5° kernel of the reach templates (the raw MC is noisier than a week of data). Cosmics and EPC (< 1 %) are left out. The X17 is Geant4 m = 16.7, measured (red) and truth (green) angles, same events. lnl/sim/lnl_week.py.

Significance. All Asimov (expected) and statistical only. Counting: the window that maximises S/√B on 2° bins, IPC known exactly (the headline 1.2 d). Template fits: binned Fisher over 90–180°, signal shape fixed, the IPC components floating (lnl_geant.reach_one). The last column is counting with a 2 % uncertainty on B in the window: Z = S/√(B + ε²B²). With the M1/E1 mix free, 3σ takes 3.7 d; the fit pays for not knowing how much of the 130–172° IPC is M1 vs E1.

Not yet in: the look-elsewhere effect for a scanned mass, and the IPC shape systematic, which no MC study here constrains. The Al and CFRP per-layer scattering budget is in lnl/out/scatter/budget.csv: the chamber wall dominates, the MM window and cathode cost nothing.

ATOMKI's bump is only +25–35 %; their cuts make it visible

Truth level, acceptance-corrected: Born IPC (M1, E1) + X17 (m = 16.7) at R = 5.8×10⁻⁶, 18.15 MeV, both leptons > 2 MeV. Hover the points.

ATOMKI cuts and mix

our M1/E1 mix, ATOMKI cuts

our mix, no |y| cut (as our Geant4 headline)

pure M1 IPC

ATOMKI 2016 Fig. 4 (read off)

Not raw counts, not background-subtracted. ATOMKI plot acceptance-corrected correlations (acceptance from event-mixed singles), cosmics subtracted (2022), on a log scale. The IPC is a simulated M1+E1 curve fitted at small angles; the anomaly is data minus that curve. Their 6.8σ also assumes the IPC shape.

The bump is +35 % at 145°, not a peak. Same scattering as ours (carbon-fibre tube, 10 µm Al backing). What makes it visible: 10° bins with ~3 % errors, and cuts.

Their cut and mix give ×3.4 in S/B: |y| ≤ 0.5 ×2, a 23 % instead of 52 % E1 share ×1.7. Even so, R = 5.8×10⁻⁶ gives half their excess in our generator: their figure needs R ≈ 1.2×10⁻⁵. Our signal is the conservative end.

lnl/out/syst/atomki_repro.csv (lnl/sim/lnl_syst.py --atomki part); ATOMKI read off arXiv:1504.01527 Fig. 4

39

Details

You can't see our X17 by eye because S/B in the window is ~7 % (§0 table: per day 117 X17 against 4,139 background with big plastics). The headline days were S/√B with B known exactly, so the significance came entirely from statistics.

ATOMKI 2016 (PRL 116 042501) Fig. 4 was digitised at 300 dpi (±3 % reading error). The data sit 26 %, 35 % and 21 % above the dashed no-boson curve at 135°, 145° and 155°. Sas et al. 2022 (arXiv:2205.07744): raw correlations, cosmic background subtracted, divided by the detector response; the anomaly is "the difference of the experimental and simulated distributions", with E1 and M1 fitted below ~110°. Their E1 share at 1.10 MeV moved from 23 % (2016) to ≳ 50 % (2022).

Generators: lnl_rates.ipc_vectors (Born, nTof_x17 ipc_born) and x17_vectors, 8Be* at rest, 2×10⁶ each, weighted by Born α (ipc_alpha.csv) and the γ share. "R needed" scales R until the as-published case matches their +35 % at 145°. Leftover differences: their efficiency vs lepton energy and y, the definition of the E1 share, and the 3.9×10⁻³ IPC coefficient they quote.

Symmetric pairs: the X17 splits its energy evenly, the IPC does not

Ten days at 1 µA with big plastics, MM 15° + TOF, E_sum 13–18 MeV, 10° bins: background (grey) and X17 at the ATOMKI ratio (red). Hover the bins.

|y| = |E₁ − E₂| / (E₁ + E₂) from the two arm energies (no charge needed). An X17 at the edge angle shares its energy equally: 99 % have |y| < 0.5. The IPC at 140° is often lopsided.

|y| < 0.3 keeps 69 % of the X17 and 43 % of the IPC. Statistics barely change (S/√B ×1.2), but S/B goes ×2.6, and S/B is what systematics eat.

ATOMKI use |y| ≤ 0.5 and show the asymmetric pairs as their null check. So can we.

lnl/out/syst/ycut.csv, spectra_10d.csv

40

Details

Geant4 tables (L1 X17, L2 IPC), the same selection as the reach slide plus a cut on the measured energy asymmetry of the two arms. E₁, E₂ are SiPM + plastic + LS of each arm, so containment smears y. In 130–160°, 99 % of the X17 have measured |y| < 0.5 (truth 100 %), against ~60 % of the M1 and ~77 % of the E1 IPC. At |y| < 0.3: 69 % of the X17, 23–27 % of M1, 39–44 % of E1.

The best window shrinks to 130–146°: symmetric X17 pairs pile up at the minimum opening angle, the edge. The IPC templates are KDE-smoothed (5°). With the cut only ~170 M1 and ~1400 E1 IPC MC events are left in 130–160° for big plastics, and 12 and 112 as built. A larger L2 run is needed before quoting the as-built numbers.

Why |y| works, where the statistics go, and why it is offline

Big plastics, 1 µA, MM 15° + TOF, E_sum 13–18 MeV, Geant4. Hover the cells, curves and points.

stats only

2 % shape

+ controls

Why. An X17 is a particle of fixed mass. Its pairs reach the smallest opening angle (the ~134° edge) only when the two leptons share the energy equally. An IPC pair at 140° is a virtual photon of any mass, with any energy split. The X17 band is a line of constant pair mass (blue, left): next slide.

Where the statistics go. |y| < 0.3 keeps 69 of 99 X17 but only 519 of 1,197 background a day (130–160°). S/√B barely changes (statistics-only days 1.07 → 0.76). S/B goes 8 → 19 %, so a shape error costs 14 → 4.3 d.

Offline, not trigger. The trigger stays the two-arm leg coincidence; E₁ and E₂ are recorded for every pair. The cut is chosen after the run, and the rejected pairs are the control sample. Fix it blind (on Monte Carlo, 441 keV, asymmetric pairs), not by tuning on the 140° bump.

lnl/out/syst/y_theta_map.csv, y_window.csv, y_scan.csv (lnl/sim/lnl_syst.py)

41

Details

|y| is computed from the two arms' measured energies (SiPM bar + plastic + LS), so it needs no charge sign and no magnetic field. The arm energies contain the leptons only partly, so measured |y| is smeared. Still, 99 % of X17 pairs in 130–160° have |y| < 0.5, and about half of the IPC has |y| > 0.3. The left map is X17/background per 5° × 0.05 cell (cells with < 0.5 background a day left blank). The best cells sit at 130–145° and |y| < 0.2.

The scan (right): statistics alone barely care about the cut between 0.3 and 0.5 (the X17 lives below 0.45). With a 2 % unknown structure in the IPC shape (Gaussian process, ℓ = 10°), the best is 0.2–0.3. The asymmetric pairs that the cut throws away are then used as a control (green), which brings the robust number back to the statistics-only one. The background includes the γ₀ IPC anisotropy about the beam (a₂ = 0.36, Hayes et al. 2021).

Because the cut is offline, nothing is lost by choosing it later. The one rule is to fix it without looking at the signal region, or to quote the look-elsewhere/trials cost of scanning it.

Why it works. W = 18.15 MeV is known, so θ and y give the pair mass, m_ee² = W²(1 − y²)(1 − cos θ)/2. The X17 edge in θ becomes a peak (FWHM ≈ 0.6 MeV); a smooth shape error cannot fake a peak. y is a ratio: the energy scale cancels.

The same idea as ATOMKI's mass fit (their Fig. 5); the |y| cut was its crude projection. Still offline: same trigger, same recorded E₁, E₂, θ.

New sensitivity: the arm-to-arm energy calibration (it moves y). Small for symmetric pairs; not yet in the fit.

lnl/out/syst/ladder_mass.csv, spectra_10d_mass.csv (lnl/sim/lnl_syst.py, use_var("mass"))

42

Details

m_ee² = W² (1 − y²)(1 − cos θ)/2 for massless leptons sharing W = 18.15 MeV (the 1.10 MeV run; E* = 18.22 MeV with the direct-capture share, a 0.4 % shift). θ = the reconstructed chord angle, y = (E₁ − E₂)/(E₁ + E₂) from the arms. The X17 (m = 16.7) reconstructs at 16.6 MeV with FWHM ≈ 0.6 MeV. The IPC γ₀ is a falling continuum with no structure at 16–17 MeV, and the γ₁ (15.1 MeV transitions) pile up below 15.

The fit is the same Asimov/Fisher ladder as the Systematics slide, now on 0.25 MeV bins over 8–20 MeV. Nuisances: M1/E1/γ₁ norms, γ* anisotropy, resolution and E scale, a cubic acceptance in m_ee, and 2 % Gaussian-process structure with ℓ ≈ 0.55 MeV (= 10° at the edge). In-run control: the γ₁ E_sum side band. All pairs; no |y| cut is needed.

Caveats: the IPC templates in m_ee are KDE-smoothed (0.27 MeV) from limited Monte Carlo; the L7 large-angle samples (×10–20 statistics) replace them. An arm-to-arm gain mismatch shifts y and smears the peak; it has to be calibrated (the 441 keV, 17.64 MeV pairs reconstruct with the same shape).

θ, all pairs: a 2 % unknown wiggle in the IPC shape turns 1.1 d into 14 d with big plastics, and 14 d into 1,587 d as built: at S/B ≈ 7 % shape error looks like signal.

m_ee: the X17 is a narrow peak on a smooth continuum, so the same 2 % costs little: 0.9 d big plastics, 9.4 d as built; with the γ₁ side band 0.8 d and 8.0 d.

lnl/out/syst/ladder.csv (lnl/sim/lnl_syst.py)

43

Details

Asimov/Fisher on 2° bins, 90–180°, background-only expectation; σ(R) from the inverse Fisher matrix with priors added. Rows, cumulative unless marked:

  • counting: S/√B in the best ≥ 10° window, B exact (the old headline).
  • fit, shape exact: one IPC normalisation and one γ₁ normalisation free.
  • M1, E1, γ₁ free: the resonant/direct mix is learned from the data (its own large-angle shape).
  • calibrated detector: angular-resolution scale ±10 % (reco − truth scaled), E_sum scale ±2 %, and a multiplicative acceptance 1 + Σaₙ Pₙ(x), n = 1–3, ±2 % each.
  • acceptance free: the same cubic with no prior.
  • unknown structure δ: a Gaussian process on the IPC shape (relative amplitude δ, correlation length 10° ≈ the X17 peak width). These are the "detector effects and contributions we aren't expecting". At ℓ = 5° it mimics the sharp X17 edge.
  • in-run controls: the asymmetric pairs (|y| ≥ 0.3) and the γ₁ E_sum side band (9–13 MeV) of the same run. They share the 2 % structure, the acceptance cubic, the resolution and E scales and the M1/E1/γ₁ norms. Each also gets 1 % structure of its own (the transfer error) and ±5 % normalisation (the MC category split). For "all pairs" only the γ₁ side band is available.
  • 441 keV: a ¼-length run on the 17.64 MeV resonance, no X17 assumed; counted in the beam days.

Mass 16.7, Li₂O 300 µg/cm² at 1.10 MeV, MM 15° + TOF, E_sum 13–18 (big plastics) / 13–17 (as built), DREAM live time included. The as-built IPC templates rest on few MC events (12 M1 in 130–160° at |y| < 0.3): treat that column as indicative.

With symmetric pairs and in-run controls, shape errors cost little

Days to 3σ against the size of unknown structure in the background shape (Gaussian process, ℓ = 10°). Hover the points.

big plastics

as built

solid: |y| < 0.3 · dashed: all pairs

open: signal run only · filled: + in-run controls

The controls come free with the run: asymmetric pairs (|y| ≥ 0.3, no X17: ATOMKI's own null check) and the γ₁ side band (15 MeV pairs at lower E_sum). They see the same detector, so they measure the acceptance shape.

441 keV (17.64 MeV) is the physics null: ATOMKI 2016 saw nothing there, 2022 "much smaller". It adds little to the shape. 0.80 MeV is not a null: ATOMKI 2022 claim the X17 in direct capture.

Event mixing (singles from different events, as ATOMKI) measures the two-arm geometric acceptance without pair correlations. That would be a third handle, not modelled here.

lnl/out/syst/delta_scan.csv (lnl/sim/lnl_syst.py)

44

Details

Same fit as the ladder (M1/E1/γ₁ free, ±10 % resolution, ±2 % E scale, acceptance cubic free). "Signal run only": the structure δ is unconstrained except by the signal category itself. "+ in-run controls": δ is shared by the signal category, the asymmetric pairs and the γ₁ side band; each has its own δ/2 structure (the transfer error) and ±5 % normalisation. As built, all pairs: past δ ≈ 1 % no amount of beam reaches 3σ in a year.

What δ to expect: the template MC alone (KDE, 5°) carries ~3–5 % per bin with today's L2 statistics. A real analysis needs ×10–100 more IPC MC, and an acceptance check from event mixing and the 441 keV run.

Two checks on the background shape: the γ* anisotropy and event mixing

Geant4 L7 IPC, big plastics. Left: true pair acceptance / event-mixing estimate, normalised over 125–175°. Hover the curves.

γ* anisotropy a₂ = 0.36: IPC in the window vs side band

big plasticsM1 IPCE1 IPC
θ, all pairs+3 %+6 %
θ, |y| < 0.3+10 %+10 %
m_ee, all pairs+8 %+9 %

Anisotropy. ⁷Li(p,γ₀) photons are not isotropic about the beam: σ(0°)/σ(150°) = 7.6 at 1.10 MeV (Zahnow 1995, M1–E1 interference) and a₂ ≈ 0.36 (Hayes et al. 2021). The interference (P₁) cancels in arms symmetric about 90°; the P₂ term reshapes the IPC by the amounts above. In the fit: a₁ ± 0.3, a₂ ± 0.15.

Event mixing (ATOMKI's method) gets the smooth tilt wrong by up to ~20 % (M1: the soft lepton's efficiency depends on its energy), but after a free cubic, mixing single-arm events matches the true acceptance to 1.2–2.6 % per 5° (big plastics): the local structure the fit allows (δ = 2 %). Mixing legs of triggered pairs is worse (1.4–4.7 %). So: a prescaled single-arm trigger, and the tilt floats in the fit.

lnl/out/syst/aniso.csv; lnl/out/mixing/ (lnl/sim/lnl_mixing.py)

45

Details

Anisotropy. W(θ_k) = 1 + a₁P₁ + a₂P₂ in the angle θ_k between the γ* (e⁺ + e⁻ momentum) and the beam, applied event by event to the γ₀ IPC Monte Carlo. a₁ ≈ 1.0 from Zahnow's 0°/150° ratio (7.6 ± 1.3 at 1100 keV) is the E1–M1 interference; it cancels for an acceptance symmetric about 90° (Hayes, Friar, Hale, Garvey, arXiv:2106.06834), and the Geant4 tables confirm ⟨P₁⟩ ≈ 0 in every bin. a₂: Hayes et al.'s R-matrix gives 4πσ(90°)/σ_int = 1 − a₂/2 = 0.82, so a₂ = 0.36; the physical range is 0–0.5. The table gives the change of the IPC in the window relative to the side band (θ: 90–120°; m_ee: 12–15 MeV).

Mixing. True acceptance = selected / generated Born in truth θ, at the two-arm trigger level (no E_sum, no pointing): the geometric part. Singles = one-arm hits from the 8Be γ-line runs (Compton and conversion electrons), the stand-in for a single-arm trigger. Mixing pair legs works for E1 but not for M1: M1 pairs at large angles are lopsided in energy, and the soft lepton's efficiency depends on its energy, which mixing cannot see. With |y| < 0.3 (both leptons hard) the singles agree for M1 too. The energy-dependent part of the efficiency has to come from Monte Carlo, checked on the 441 keV run.

Take every single-arm trigger, with the prescale ready: it costs a few % of live time

DREAM RAW (τ = 298 µs, 20 samples), Geant4 8Be γ singles + cosmics, Li₂O at 1.04 MeV. Hover the points.

The logic: each arm's leg (SiPM bar AND plastic ≥ 0.5 MIP) is a trigger. Two outputs into DREAM: PAIR (≥ 2 legs in 20 ns) never prescaled, and SINGLE (≥ 1 leg) prescaled 1/P, plus a 1 Hz clock. The trigger word (legs, output, prescale counter) goes with each event.

What singles buy: cosmic MIPs per arm for the gain (1,138/h even at P = 10: ~1 % per hour, so σ_g ≈ 1–2 % is easy); the event-mixing acceptance (§13.3); per-arm efficiency maps; and the 8Be γ single-arm spectra as a high-energy check of the scale.

P = 1 up to ~2–4 µA. Above that, P = 2–10 keeps 95 %. Pairs, the physics, lose only the live time. Not included: ¹⁹F(p,αγ) on a LiF target (ask).

lnl/out/trigger/prescale.csv, prescale_choice.csv (lnl/sim/lnl_trigger.py)

46

Details

Rates from lnl_geant.singles: per-arm legs per γ of each 8Be line (L3) and per second of cosmics (L4). Pair rate = correlated two-arm legs + 20 ns accidentals. Single-only events ≈ legs − 2 × pairs. Live = 1/(1 + fτ), non-paralysable, the same for both outputs, so the prescale protects the pairs only through the live time. Data: 83 MB/s per FEU at 3.35 kHz, ~25 kB per event per FEU.

The gain precision per hour uses σ(MPV)/MPV ≈ 0.35/√N for a Landau ⊗ Gauss with σ/MPV ≈ 0.2 (the n_TOF 2 cm bars) and the weakest arm's cosmic rate. Per bar it is ×√(bars per arm) worse, still ≲ 1 % per day.

Offline, the single-arm sample is exactly normalised for any P. A design rule follows: never let a prescale touch the PAIR output, and keep P a run-condition parameter, not a firmware constant.

Big plastics survive: 0.8 d ideal → 1.4 d calibrated, 2.4 d with n_TOF-quality calibration, 5.0 d with poor plates. The m_ee peak barely widens: 5 cm stops the soft lepton and catches most of the hard one.

As built does not: 8.0 d → 35 d even with a repaired liquid, 191 d as at n_TOF, 491 d without it. 2 cm of plastic stops neither lepton, so y and E_sum rest on a 18 mm liquid cell and ~10 photoelectrons/MeV. Split: plastic + SiPM real, LS ideal → 23 d; LS real only → 18 d; an LS at a = 0.2 → 31 d.

Gains are not the problem: a per-arm gain nuisance costs ≤ 15 % even at σ_g = 10 % (big plastics); single-arm cosmics give 1–2 % anyway.

lnl/out/calo/days.csv, resolution.csv, spectra.csv, ls_scan.csv (lnl/sim/lnl_calo.py)

47

Details

The response (lnl/sim/lnl_calo.py), per arm and layer: E(1 + c·N) + a√E·N′, zero below threshold. From n_TOF (nTof_x17/ntof_calorimetry, C1 and C4):

  • 2 cm plastic bars: the cosmic MIP (3.41 MeV) has a Gauss σ/MPV of 0.13–0.24 per bar. The scint-stack per-cell maps spread 4–5 % (arm B 9.5 %). Model: a = 0.32 √MeV, c = 5 % (2 % with an MM-position map). The n_TOF scale is known to ~10 % (MIP vs source line 3–24 % apart).
  • SiPM wall: a = 0.19 √MeV (25 % at the 0.6 MeV MIP), c = 8 % / 4 %.
  • Liquid: MIP σ/MPV 0.46, 6–9 mV/MeV against a 16–18 mV zero suppression (1.8–2.8 MeV threshold), MIP efficiency 14–56 % and position-dependent. n_TOF model: threshold 2.3 MeV, a = 0.78, log-normal light collection σ = 0.5. Repaired: threshold 0.5, a = 0.5, c = 15 %.
  • 5 cm big plates: no data. a = 0.20–0.35 √MeV, c = 5–15 %.

The per-arm gain error goes into the fit as four nuisances (σ_g: 10 % n_TOF as is, 2 % calibrated with single-arm cosmics, 5 % poor plates). The E_sum window is re-chosen for each response: e.g. 14–19 MeV with big plastics.

Not modelled: Birks quenching of stopping electrons (a few %); the SiPM-wall leg efficiency (75–91 % unbiased at n_TOF, ×1.2–1.8 in days if it stays); a non-linear plastic above 5 MeV (n_TOF checked linearity only to 1.45 MIP).

More discovery power once the energies are real. With the calibrated response the m_ee peak is smeared by the y resolution, but θ, |y| and E_sum each still separate. m_ee alone 1.7 d → m_ee × |y| 1.1 d → θ × |y| × E_sum 1.0 d with big plastics; as built 41 → 22 → 17 d.

And robust where 1D is not. The worst structure tried (5 %, edge-like, in m_ee) takes m_ee alone to 3.1 d (big plastics) and 529 d (as built); the 3D fit stays at 1.2 and 21 d. The X17 is a curve in (θ, |y|) at fixed E_sum; acceptance structure is a band in θ, a γ₁ leak a band in E_sum, a shape error in m_ee a diagonal: the fit tells them apart.

The angle-only fits are fragile: with a free acceptance cubic their days swing ×2–3 between the two halves of the Monte Carlo. The 2D and 3D fits agree between halves to ≲ 10 %.

Nothing new to record: θ, E₁, E₂ are in every pair event. The E_sum axis replaces the γ₁ side-band cut by a fit; the |y| axis replaces the |y| cut and keeps the asymmetric pairs as the control inside the same fit.

lnl/out/nd/nd_days_*.csv (lnl/sim/lnl_nd.py)

48

Details

lnl/sim/lnl_nd.py. The unknown structure is a weight 1 + Σcⱼφⱼ on every background event, with φⱼ the Gaussian-process modes in physical variables: S_θ in the reconstructed angle (acceptance, geometry: the same at every |y| and E_sum), S_m in m_ee (the §13 assumption), S_θy local in the (θ, |y|) plane (a background-physics shape error), all ℓ = 10° (0.55 MeV, 0.15 in |y|). Each analysis sees the same structure through its own binning, so the columns compare like with like.

Every fit floats M1, E1, γ₁ norms, the anisotropy, resolution and E scale, a free acceptance cubic in θ, a |y| tilt (±5 %), the four arm gains and the |y| resolution. The θ-only fit is near-degenerate with the free cubic: its days swing ×2–3 between MC halves. The 2D and 3D fits agree between halves to ≲ 10 %. Templates are KDE-smoothed (5° or 0.27 MeV) along their first axis; |y| (6 bins) and E_sum (4 bins: two in the γ₁ side band, two in the window) are plain bins.

The 1D m_ee here (no in-run controls, acceptance cubic in θ rather than in m_ee) is a little slower than the Calorimetry slide's m_ee fit (γ₁ side band as a control). The 3D fit contains that control as its E_sum axis.

A month at 1 µA reaches ×1.3 below the ATOMKI claim as built, ×5 with big plastics

The X17 ratio R on one log axis: ATOMKI's claim, MEG II's null, and MX17's 3σ reach after 30 days at 1 µA (Geant4). Hover the points.

The record is contradictory. ATOMKI (2016, 2022) and Hanoi (2024) see ~140° excesses; MEG II (2025) sees nothing; MEG II members (Sept 2026) show cosmics make a 140° bump in ATOMKI-type spectrometers.

What MX17 adds: tracks + timing that remove cosmics, and with big plastics ~9× ATOMKI's pair acceptance (as built, about equal: 3.3 % vs ~2.5 %). LNL's own 2023–24 data (unpublished) are the other result to wait for.

MX17 points: lnl/out/nd/nd_days_*.csv (MM 15° + TOF, calibrated response, θ × |y| × E_sum fit, S_θ 2 % + S_θy 1 %).

Appendix · the basics, for someone new to proton beams

How a proton-beam X17 measurement works, from the accelerator to the opening angle

Each slide answers one question and points back to the main slide it explains. Hover the dotted terms and every drawn element; the Details drop-downs carry the numbers and sources.

A · The beam

how a Van de Graaff makes it; energy, time structure; protons vs neutrons; the rate chain

→

B · The target

thin vs stopping targets (slide 6); why we count photons; the chamber and its scattering

→

C · The physics

capture and de-excitation like ³He; where the beam energy goes (E*); M1/E1/E0; the X17 bump; kinematics; off-resonance

→

D · Glossary

every acronym in the deck

The short answers

Beam: one energy you dial in (0.2–2 MeV on AN2000), ~1 keV wide, continuous, 6×10¹² protons/s per µA. No neutrons below 1.88 MeV.

Target: thin, so the beam spends only 1.10 → 1.04 MeV in lithium. A target that stops the beam makes 77 % of its pairs at 17.64 MeV, where there is no X17.

Chamber: needed for the vacuum; its wall sets the angular resolution (5.1° for 0.4 mm CFRP). ~4° is reachable with a thinner or wider wall.

Physics: like ³He, capture then de-excitation. No useful boost (β = 0.006); the X17's own speed sets the ~134° edge, which drops as E_p rises. Off resonance is a test, not more X17.

51

Details

Written 2026-10-08 for readers new to the ⁸Be channel and to proton beams. Everything quantitative comes from lnl_rates.py (cross sections, stopping, yields), lnl/appendix_calc.py (depth profiles, scattering model, decay kinematics, off-resonance yields) or the Geant4 tables of the main deck. Analytic stand-ins are labelled as such.

A Van de Graaff gives one proton energy, set by a voltage

Schematic of a single-ended electrostatic accelerator like AN2000 or CN (not to scale). Hover the parts.

Choose any E_p in 0.2–2.0 MeV on AN2000 (0.8–5.5 on CN). Self-service AN2000: one change per day, which suits a plan of a few energies held for days.

Continuous (DC): protons arrive at random, 6.2×10¹² /s at 1 µA. CN can also pulse: 2 ns every 333 ns (≤ 700 nA).

Energy calibration on known narrow lines: the 441 keV resonance itself, ²⁷Al(p,γ) at 992 keV, the ⁷Li(p,n) threshold at 1.881 MeV.

Main slide 3 (Beam) gives the machine ranges. lnl/FACILITY.md

52

Details

An electrostatic accelerator keeps one electrode (the terminal) at a steady high voltage V. Ions are made inside the terminal and fall to ground through the accelerating tube, gaining q·V. For protons (q = e), E_p in MeV equals V in MV. There is no RF and no bunching, so the beam is continuous.

The analysing magnet is what fixes the energy precisely. It passes only one momentum per charge onto the slits, and the slit currents correct V. The LNL sheet quotes σ_E/E ~ 10⁻³ for CN (~1 keV at 1 MeV); AN2000 is not quoted (ask), but it is the same kind of machine. 1 keV is small compared to the target thickness (~60 keV in 300 µg/cm² Li₂O) and to the 168 keV width of the 18.15 MeV resonance, though not to the 12 keV of the 441 keV one.

Contamination: the source also makes H₂⁺ (two protons at E/2 each) and H₃⁺. A properly tuned analysing magnet removes them. MEG II's Cockcroft–Walton beam had 25 % H₂⁺ and put most of its data on 441 keV (TARGETS.md §6). Specify H⁺ only.

Sources: LNL beam sheet (refs/LNL_Beams_AN2000_CN.txt), CN paper arXiv:2605.12005, lnl/FACILITY.md.

One energy at a time, all the time: the opposite of n_TOF

Left: energies each beam delivers (log scale). Right: when the particles arrive. Hover the bars.

No time of flight needed: E_p is known from the machine. The only energy spread that matters is the ~60 keV lost in the film.

Beam off = pure cosmics: with a DC beam you measure the cosmic background directly by switching the beam off.

CN pulsed: a pair must arrive in a 2 ns window every 333 ns, a ×~50 cut on cosmics.

LNL beam sheet; CN paper arXiv:2605.12005. Energy bands are ranges, not flux shapes.

53

Details

Energy. n_TOF gives every energy at once and sorts them afterwards by time of flight; most of the beam is at energies the X17 does not want. The ILL gives one energy (thermal). LNL gives one energy that we choose. There is no "yield spectrum" of the beam itself: it is a line. What has a spectrum is the reaction as the beam slows inside the target (A6, and main slide 4 for σ(E_p)).

Time. A continuous beam means no beam-off window to measure cosmics in, but also no instantaneous rate spikes: at 1 µA the two-arm trigger rate is a few per second, dominated by cosmics (main slide 12). CN's pulsed mode is a cosmic and accidental veto nobody has used for ⁸Be yet (a pair must arrive in the 2 ns window): ×~50 against cosmics in PHYSICS.md §4.

n_TOF numbers are the facility's standard ones (20 GeV/c PS bunches of ~7 ns, ≥ 1.2 s apart); they are here only for contrast.

Protons stop in microns: thin targets, vacuum, no neutrons

What changes when the beam is protons instead of neutrons. Hover the dotted terms.

neutrons (n_TOF, ILL)protons (LNL)
what the beam does in the targetno charge: flies straight until it is captured or scattersionises continuously: loses ~20 keV per 100 µg/cm², stops in ~17 µm of Al
so the target isthick: the ILL ³He cell absorbs 99.5 % of the beamthin: a ~1.5 µm film that only ~60 keV of the beam energy is spent in; the beam goes on to a dump
fraction of beam that makes a 20 MeV γ1.03×10⁻⁸ per absorbed n3.0×10⁻¹⁰ per proton (γ₀)
20 MeV-class γ per second~196/s at the ILL (1.9×10¹⁰ n/s absorbed)~1,848/s at 1 µA (γ₀ only; γ₁ adds 2×)
why the cross section is smallradiative capture competes with (n,p), which is 10⁸× biggerCoulomb barrier: σ(p,γ₀) ~ 20–30 µb near 1 MeV
beam-made background in the detectoryes, the dominant one: stray neutrons captured everywhere (MM occupancy, accidentals)almost none: no neutrons below 1.881 MeV; γ from other nuclei (¹⁹F, ²⁷Al, ¹¹B) and the dump. Cosmics dominate.
beam pathair or He is fine; windowsvacuum all the way to the target, so a chamber wall the leptons must cross (B3)
normalisationflux monitors, simulated beam profilethe charge on the Faraday cup: protons counted directly
what wears outthe gas cell leaks ³He1.1 W/µA of heat, implanted hydrogen, Li diffusion: replace targets ~weekly

54

Details

The headline difference is that a proton beam interacts with every electron it passes, so it slows down and stops, while a neutron beam passes through matter almost freely until it is captured. Three consequences run through the whole deck:

  1. The target has to be thin, and its thickness sets which ⁸Be energies are made (B1).
  2. The beam has to be in vacuum, so there is a chamber whose wall scatters the leptons (B3–B4).
  3. The beam does not fill the hall with neutrons. At the ILL the stray neutrons set the walls on rate (MM occupancy, accidentals). Here the beam-related background is tiny and the cosmics are what is left (main slides 9 and 12).

The ILL rate is R_MAX 1.9×10¹⁰ n/s (the Ø2 cm spot) × 1.03×10⁻⁸; the ILL also has the M1/E0 pair channels at a similar α. The LNL rate is the ATOMKI-2016 target at 1 µA from out/yields.csv. Ranges: PSTAR (lnl/data/pstar_stopping.csv). ILL numbers: ill/FEASIBILITY_SIM.md.

1 proton in 3×10⁹ makes an 18 MeV γ; ~6 X17/day survive

Per day at 1 µA, ATOMKI-2016 target (Li₂O 300 µg/cm², 1.10 MeV), n_TOF hardware as built. Log bars; hover them.

Every step after the γ₀ is a fixed fraction of it. That is why the main deck counts photons: γ₀ per second is the unit everything scales with (B2).

55

Details

Each bar is the previous physics bar times one factor. Protons → γ₀ is the thin-target yield (cross section × ⁷Li atoms per cm², integrated as the beam slows through the film). γ₀ → IPC is the Born internal-conversion coefficient α at 18.15 MeV (out/ipc_alpha.csv), weighted by the resonance (M1) and direct-capture (E1) shares. γ₀ → X17 is the ATOMKI ratio R. The detector bars are the Geant4 chain of main slide 7 and the per-day budget of main slide 10.

A stopping target walks the beam through 441 keV

Main slide 6 explained. Top: the two targets. Left: proton energy against depth. Right: where that puts the beam on σ(E_p).

lnl/out/appendix/depth.csv, lnl/out/figures/excitation.csv, lnl/out/yields.csv

56

Details

"Stopping" refers to the proton beam, not to photons. A stopping (or "thick") target is one in which the protons lose all their energy. A thin target lets them through having lost only a little. Slide 6 asks: of the 18 MeV-class photons the target makes, how many come from the 441 keV resonance (and so are 17.64 MeV transitions, not 18.15)?

The answer depends only on which proton energies are spent inside lithium. In the thin film the protons go from 1100 to 1039 keV, nowhere near 441, so 0.6 % of γ₀ are 17.64 (the BW tail). In a target that stops the beam, every energy down to zero is spent in lithium. The 441 keV resonance is only 12 keV wide, but its peak is ~50× the 18.15 one, so it ends up making 77 % of all γ₀. Thin: 1,848 γ₀/s, 0.6 % at 17.64 MeV. Stopping: 143,074 γ₀/s, 77 % at 17.64 MeV.

This happened to ATOMKI in 2016: their "300 µg/cm² Li₂O" was really metallic Li diffused ~10 µm into the Al backing (Sas 2022). The fix is a stable compound (LiF, Li₂O) on a cool backing, checked during the run (478 keV PIGE line, γ₀ line width).

Curves: out/appendix/depth.csv (PSTAR stopping, the integration of lnl_rates.thin_yield). Li metal at 0.534 g/cm³; the Li₂O film at bulk density, 300 µg/cm² = 1.49 µm.

Every pair channel is a fixed fraction of the photons

What an excited ⁸Be nucleus does next, per 18 MeV photon. Hover the branches.

We never count the photons themselves. We count γ₀ because both the background (IPC = α·γ₀) and the signal (X17 = R·γ₀) are fixed fractions of it. Double the γ₀, double both.

So "77 % of γ₀ at 17.64 MeV" means 77 % of the pairs come from the wrong state. 17.64 MeV makes IPC (α = 3.4e-03) but no X17 (MEG II: R(17.6) < 1.8×10⁻⁶).

The energy sum cannot tell them apart: 17.64 and 18.15 are 0.5 MeV apart, well inside the E_sum resolution. For the same X17 a stopping target gives ×4.4 the IPC.

Tilley 2004 (A = 8); lnl/out/ipc_alpha.csv; lnl/PHYSICS.md §1

57

Details

Slides 6 and 10 of the main deck express target yields as "γ₀ per second". γ₀ is the transition to the ⁸Be ground state. It is what earlier experiments measured (Zahnow's σ(p,γ₀)), and it is the denominator of R = Γ_X/Γ_γ. The pairs follow from it: IPC is α·γ₀ with α ≈ 3.5–4.4×10⁻³ (Born, out/ipc_alpha.csv), X17 is R·γ₀.

The fraction of γ₀ from the 441 keV resonance is the fraction of the pair background that comes with no X17. That holds for ATOMKI's 2016 non-observation at 17.64 and MEG II's limit there. With 77 % of the IPC coming from 17.64, the signal-to-background in the window drops by ×4.4, and the IPC shape changes (pure M1, no E1).

γ₁ (to the broad 3.0 MeV state) is twice as frequent but 3 MeV lower. The E_sum window removes it (main slide 8).

The beam needs vacuum, and the leptons pay for the wall

Side view of the Geant4 target region with one X17 lepton crossing the chamber wall. Hover the parts.

Why a chamber at all: the beam must be in vacuum. A 1.1 MeV proton stops in ~2.7 cm of air; the film would oxidise; the beam line is pumped anyway.

What it costs: each lepton crosses the wall and scatters, by 2.6° rms in 0.4 mm CFRP and 5.5° in 0.5 mm Al (Highland, 8.6 MeV). The opening angle is the chord from the beam spot to the hit, so the kink becomes an angle error.

Geant4 (L5): X17 σ68 = 5.1° (CFRP 0.4), 8.8° (Al 0.5), 12.2° (Al 1.0). The wall is the largest single term; acceptance does not change.

The backing and holder matter less: a Cu 25 µm backing gives 7.5°, C 20 µm the same as Al 10 µm.

Geant4 L5 chamber scan: lnl/out/geant/material_scan.csv. Highland: PDG formula, plane-projected, β = 1.

58

Details

Geometry (MX17_Full_Geant lnl, --target li): Li₂O 300 µg/cm² film on Al 10 µm, Al 1 mm holder annulus at r 10–20 mm, CFRP 0.4 mm chamber tube of inner radius 25 mm and half-length 300 mm, Al 5 mm flanges, Ta 2 mm dump at +250 mm. The leptons of an X17 pair leave at ~25–155° to the beam, so each crosses the tube wall once, at ~68° on average, over a path of t/sin θ.

Why it matters: the X17 makes a sharp edge in the opening angle at ~134°. A resolution σ smears the edge over ~σ, so the analysis window has to be wider and lets more IPC in. Main slide 12 has the scan; B4 extrapolates it to other walls.

The Micromegas measure positions well (0.6–0.8 mm) and directions poorly (11–26°), so the opening angle is reconstructed as the chord from the beam spot (a point, here) to the hit. A kink at radius r moves the hit by θ·(L − r), an angle error of θ·(L − r)/L at the Micromegas (L ≈ 215 mm).

The wall can come down from 5.1° to ~4°, never below 3.5°
